scope: Official-label-only binary event proposal research; not event-type or legal-rule validation
hypothesis: Supervised local Qwen vision representations may retain useful event information that the frozen generative legal gate and DINO representations failed to expose. Temporal neighborhoods are compared with single-frame features on the same inference grid.

features.frame_representation: mean of merged visual tokens, L2 normalize, fixed Gaussian projection, L2 normalize
features.temporal: concatenate current, previous-current and next-current representations; boundary repeat

head.positive_training: only nearest grid center to official TRAIN point; no oracle-centered extraction
head.negative_training: all grid centers in official negative TRAIN videos
head.weights: equal mass per video within each class; classes equal total mass
head.video_pooling: maximum score on fixed grid; argmax supplies candidate timestamp
head.validation: leave one automatic TRAIN duplicate group out; scaler fitted inside each fold

budget.preflight_selection: shortest, median and longest TRAIN duration; label-blind

acceptance.temporal_advantage: balanced accuracy >= static + 0.05 OR timestamp MAE <= static - 1 second with no F1 regression

stopping: No parameter, feature, threshold or seed search after results. Failed technical probe or TRAIN gate ends QVT-01; TUNE and HOLDOUT stay closed. No deployment based only on binary proposal quality.
limitations: Automatic groups are not expert scene-family groups
Point labels are not exhaustive event intervals
Previously explored TRAIN data; OOF is exploratory, not a fresh final estimate
Image encoder neighborhoods do not guarantee action understanding
